# Parameters
## 1) Security’s priority Security’s priority should be at all times to prevent loss of life and property destruction aboard the station. Security are not police. They do not have the authority of GALPOL to enforce the full extent of the law. Space law is, therefore, a truncated version of Solarian Law that Security, as a private security force, are licensed to enforce.
## 2) Security’s jurisdiction is limited Security’s jurisdiction is limited to a 100-meter radius around all corporate-owned facilities, including the station, lavaland outpost, and High-Mass Mining Claim (“VGroid” or “Red Rock”). Security’s jurisdiction also covers the Automated Trade station (ATS) and all shuttles owned by corporate facilities, including shuttles purchased, constructed, or claimed during any shift. Should events transpire that require an extension of this range, Central Command must be contacted for guidance.
Security may pursue immediate threats that have encroached on the station outside of this range. The Head of Security and/or the Captain should be informed before doing so. Security must return to station if requested by the Captain or Head of Security as soon as possible. Security must always prioritise the station over the pursuit.
## 3) The command structure of security The command structure of security is as follows: Captain/Acting Commanding Officer -> Head of Security -> Warden -> Security Officers (including Corpsman, Detective, Security Technician, and Mentors) -> Security Cadets
### In cases of medical emergency within security The command structure is altered as follows: Captain/Acting Commanding Officer -> Head of Security -> Warden -> Corpsman -> Security Mentors and Security Officers (including Detective and Security Technicians) -> Security Cadets - Medical emergencies within security include medical emergencies involving permas and other prisoners.
### In regards to actions taken regarding ongoing criminal investigations In regards to actions taken regarding ongoing criminal investigations only, the command structure is altered as follows: Captain/Acting Commanding Officer -> Head of Security -> Warden -> Detective -> Security Mentors and Security Officers (including Corpsman and Security Technicians) -> Security Cadets - Ongoing criminal investigations include such items as: finding evidence, interrogating suspects, and searching suspects. - Ongoing criminal investigations (and their appropriate chain of command) do not take priority over emergencies that endanger the entire station (such as Code Yellow, active Nuclear Operatives threat, Code Violet).
### Security Mentors do not have jurisdiction over Security Officers Security Mentors do not have jurisdiction over Security Officers (including Detective, Corpsman, or Security Technician) except in matters pertaining to mentoring either them, or mentoring cadets. Security Mentors should always prioritize the training of cadets and, upon request, other security department members.
# Definitions
## Active Carry Active carrying is when a weapon is carried in the hand of the officer for transport purposes (not ongoing combat). - Carrying a rifle on the back is not active carrying. - Carrying a sidearm in its holster is not active carrying.
## Armor Any equipment that, when worn, provides at least 20% protection from two or more of the following damage types: Blunt, Pierce, Slash, Heat, Explosion
## Arresting Officer The officer that has placed cuffs on a suspect or arrestee and brought them to security. If this is two different officers for any reason, the officer who witnessed more of the situation is the arresting officer.
## Contraband Any equipment or item that is illegal to possess on board a station.
## Heavy Weapon Any weapon that slows the wielder down when carried in two hands, fires explosive ordinance, or is anchored in place for operation. - Automated, energy-based “Sentry Turrets” are not heavy weapons.
## Longarm Any firearm, regardless of lethality or make, that cannot be stowed in a boot or pocket.
## Restricted Item Any equipment or item that is legal to possess by certain personnel or departments.
## Security/Security Department/Security Members The Head of Security, and all crew members who report directly to the Head of Security.
## Sidearm Any firearm, regardless of lethality or make, that can be stowed within a boot or pocket. - The Advanced Laser Pistol is considered a sidearm, despite its inability to be stored in a boot or pocket.
## Warrant An official piece of paperwork that gives jurisdiction to carry out an arrest or a search. All warrants require signatures to be valid.
